q: Painters are exposed to technical-grade xylene, which contains ethylbenzene. According to the ACGIH BEI documentation, why does the xylene BEI (methylhippuric acids in urine) apply only to technical or commercial xylenes?
options: Ethylbenzene slows conversion of xylenes to the metabolites.
Pure xylene isomers are not metabolized to methylhippuric acids.
Ethylbenzene increases xylene excretion and inflates the result.
Technical-grade xylene is not absorbed through the skin.
explain: Ethylbenzene, present in technical and commercial xylene, inhibits the metabolism of xylenes to methylhippuric acids. The BEI was derived for the mixtures workers actually encounter, so it applies to technical or commercial grades only. B: All xylene isomers are metabolized to the corresponding methylhippuric acids. C: Ethylbenzene reduces rather than increases methylhippuric acid formation. D: Xylene can be absorbed through the skin regardless of grade.

q: Indoor and outdoor air samples for fungi are collected during an indoor air quality investigation. Which comparison is most informative?
options: Total indoor spore counts against a published numerical limit
The rank order of genera indoors against control and outdoor samples
Indoor counts against the counts measured on the previous visit
Indoor counts against the counts in a nearby unaffected building
explain: There is no health-based numerical limit for airborne fungi, so interpretation rests on comparison. Examining the rank order of genera in complaint-area samples against control areas and outdoor samples reveals whether an indoor amplification source is present, which a total count alone cannot do. A: No authoritative numerical limit exists for airborne fungal concentrations. C: Day-to-day variation in outdoor fungal levels makes a comparison across visits unreliable. D: Another building has its own sources and outdoor exposure and is a weaker control than same-day outdoor and non-complaint samples.

q: Several office workers are diagnosed with hypersensitivity pneumonitis linked to a contaminated humidifier, with abnormal chest imaging and lung function. How should this situation be classified?
options: Sick building syndrome
Mass psychogenic illness
Building-related illness
Multiple chemical sensitivity
explain: Building-related illness (BRI) has an established etiology and a distinguishable set of symptoms, often with physical signs and clinical abnormalities, such as hypersensitivity pneumonitis or Legionnaires' disease. Sick building syndrome describes symptoms without an identifiable cause or clinical findings. A: Sick building syndrome lacks a specific etiology and clinical abnormalities. B: Mass psychogenic illness is not supported by the objective clinical findings. D: Multiple chemical sensitivity is a separate, poorly defined condition.

q: A Legionella assessment reports positive results in the domestic hot and cold water systems of a building. Which conclusion about the cooling tower is supported?
options: The cooling tower is also colonised, since the systems share a supply
The cooling tower is uncolonised, since it was not reported positive
The tower requires no assessment once the domestic systems are remediated
No conclusion is supported, because the tower was outside the sampling scope
explain: Findings extend only to the systems actually sampled. A report of positive domestic hot and cold water results supports no inference either way about a cooling tower that was not within the sampling scope, and the tower would need its own assessment on its own merits. A: Shared make-up water does not establish colonisation of a separate system with different conditions. B: Absence from a report is not a negative result; the system was not examined. C: Remediating the domestic systems does not characterise or control a separate tower.

q: Early in an exposure assessment programme, few quantitative data exist. How does the AIHA strategy characterize the exposure profiles developed at that stage?
options: Mostly qualitative, to be modified as information accumulates
Invalid until at least ten measurements are available
Equivalent in confidence to profiles based on measurement
Final once documented, with no later revision expected
explain: Early in the process few quantitative data may be available, so most early exposure profiles will be based on qualitative information. As the information gathering and assessing cycle progresses, similar exposure groups may be redefined and their profiles modified based on new information. B: Qualitative profiles are used to prioritize work rather than being invalid. C: Qualitative profiles carry lower confidence than measured profiles. D: Profiles are revised as new information becomes available.

q: A slot hood is designed for a slot velocity of 2,000 fpm. What is the maximum plenum velocity that should be specified?
options: 500 fpm
explain: The maximum slot hood plenum velocity should be half the slot velocity, so 1,000 fpm for a 2,000 fpm slot. Keeping the plenum velocity low ensures that the pressure drop across the slot, not the plenum, governs the distribution, which is what makes the airflow uniform along the slot. A: 500 fpm is more conservative than required and enlarges the plenum unnecessarily. C: 2,000 fpm would equal the slot velocity and destroy the uniformity of distribution. D: 4,000 fpm far exceeds the design criterion.

q: What should an inspection practice for issued chemical gloves require?
options: Replacement on a fixed annual schedule regardless of use
Inspection only when a worker reports a chemical burn
Inspection before each use, with removal of degraded gloves
Laboratory permeation testing of each pair before issue
explain: Gloves are inspected before use, and those that are discoloured, stiff, swollen, or perforated are removed from service, since such changes indicate excessive use or chemical degradation. A fixed calendar interval neither catches early failures nor avoids discarding serviceable items. A: A calendar interval ignores the actual conditions of use. B: Waiting for an injury means the control has already failed. D: Routine laboratory testing of issued gloves is impractical; published data informs selection.

q: A contractor will perform maintenance inside a plant. What does coordination of the procurement process require?
options: Verifying the contractor insurance cover before entry
Requiring the contractor to accept all liability in the contract
Limiting the contractor to work outside production hours
Identifying hazards from both the contractor and plant activities
explain: The organisation coordinates its procurement process with contractors in order to identify hazards and to assess and control risks arising both from the activities of the contractors that affect the organisation and from the activities of the organisation that affect the workers of the contractor. The duty runs in both directions. A: Insurance is a commercial safeguard and not a control over the work. B: Liability clauses allocate cost after an event rather than controlling the risk. C: Scheduling may reduce interaction but does not identify or control the hazards.

q: Why does a worker in a mildly oxygen-deficient atmosphere often fail to recognise the danger and withdraw?
options: Early effects include impaired attention and judgment
The atmosphere has no detectable odour at any level
Oxygen deficiency causes immediate unconsciousness
Breathing rate falls, so the worker feels comfortable
explain: The early physiological effects of oxygen deficiency include impaired attention, judgment, and coordination along with increased breathing and heart rate, so the faculties needed to recognise the hazard and act on it are among the first affected. That is why entry controls, monitoring, and attendants are required rather than reliance on self-rescue. B: Absence of odour contributes, but the governing reason is the loss of judgment. C: Immediate unconsciousness occurs at severe deficiency rather than at mild levels. D: Breathing and heart rate increase rather than fall.

q: What does it mean for a risk assessment methodology to be proactive?
options: It responds quickly after an incident
It anticipates risk before harm occurs
It is repeated at fixed intervals
It is performed by external experts
explain: The methodology and criteria must be defined so that they are proactive rather than reactive, which means identifying and assessing risk from the work as planned and performed rather than waiting for incidents to reveal it. Fixed intervals and external involvement are separate matters. A: Rapid response after an event is reactive by definition. C: Periodicity does not make an approach proactive. D: External expertise does not determine whether the approach anticipates risk.
